# Stella Maynard

## Overview

- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v1 c35 P4](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0004), [v3 c9 P6](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0006)</sub>
- **Status:** poor  <sub>[v3 c10 P52](../source/v03-c10.md#nw-v03-c10-p0052)</sub>
- **Role:** schoolteacher and student  <sub>[v3 c9 P7](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0007), [v3 c16 P4](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0004)</sub>
- **Titles:** rose-red girl  <sub>[v1 c35 P4](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0004)</sub>

## Appearance

Stella is a vivid, black-eyed girl who carried off the palm for beauty in her Second Year classes at Queen's Academy.

_Sources: [v1 c35 P4](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0004), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006)_

## Personality

Stella is thoughtful, imaginative, and ambitious, possessing a heartful of wistful, aerial dreams and fancies. She appreciates the cozy comfort of living at Patty's Place with her friends, though she occasionally experiences moments of feeling blue, discouraged, and existential.

_Sources: [v1 c35 P4](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0004), [v3 c27 P10](../source/v03-c27.md#nw-v03-c27-p0010), [v3 c35 P31](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0031)_

- attend Redmond College and live with her friends at Patty's Place  <sub>[v3 c9 P6](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0006), [v3 c10 P47](../source/v03-c10.md#nw-v03-c10-p0047)</sub>

## History

While studying at Queen's Academy, Stella Maynard became intimate friends with Anne Shirley and Priscilla Grant, forming a close circle of ambitious students. After completing her studies at Queen's, where she was considered the most beautiful student in the Second Year classes, she taught school. Later, she conceived the idea of attending Redmond College and renting Patty's Place to live with Anne, Priscilla, and her aunt, who served as housekeeper. At Redmond, she joined her housemates—along with Philippa Gordon—at Patty's Place as a student, eventually earning a good all-round showing in her examinations.

_Sources: [v1 c35 P4](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0004), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006), [v3 c9 P6](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0006), [v3 c9 P7](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0007), [v3 c10 P47](../source/v03-c10.md#nw-v03-c10-p0047), [v3 c16 P0](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0000), [v3 c16 P4](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0004), [v3 c37 P29](../source/v03-c37.md#nw-v03-c37-p0029)_

## Quotes

> I’m so glad we can keep Patty’s Place for another year. I was afraid they’d come back. And then our jolly little nest here would be broken up—and we poor callow nestlings thrown out on the cruel world of boardinghouses again.  <sub>[v3 c27 P10](../source/v03-c27.md#nw-v03-c27-p0010)</sub>

> I’m blue and discouraged myself, throwing herself on the couch. Nothing seems worthwhile. My very thoughts are old. I’ve thought them all before. What is the use of living after all, Anne?  <sub>[v3 c35 P31](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0031)</sub>

> It does—but I am not jealous. I love Anne and I like Roy. Everybody says she is making a brilliant match, and even Mrs. Gardner thinks her charming now. It all sounds as if it were made in heaven, but I have my doubts. Make the most of that, Aunt Jamesina.  <sub>[v3 c38 P16](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0016)</sub>
